sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Random Forest (model_id python-random-forest) is a classifier that predicts the target default.payment.next.month using the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset. Its recorded business purpose is a benchmark model for internal analysis that is not used in decisions, but this purpose was inferred rather than confirmed. The business owner, intended use, the decisions it supports, and whether it runs in production or only as a benchmark are not documented. The development data is public demonstration data on credit-card clients in Taiwan (April to September 2005) and is not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier with n_estimators=150, random_state set to a seed (default 42), n_jobs=-1 and class_weight="balanced" to handle class imbalance. Preprocessing renames the target, drops ID, removes rows with missing values on the workbook path, casts the target to int, and uses a stratified train/test split (recorded as 0.8/0.2, with the train fraction inferred). Predictors are credit limit, education, marital status, repayment status (PAY_0 to PAY_6), bill amounts and payment amounts; ID, SEX and AGE are excluded, with SEX and AGE kept only for fairness analysis, and no feature scaling is applied. The input feature list was inferred, and the tuning rationale for n_estimators=150 with other parameters at defaults is not documented.

rows.label: Preprocessing
rows.value: Rename 'default payment next month' to default.payment.next.month and drop ID (workbook path), Drop rows with missing values (workbook path); the official UCI path is validated to have no missing values, Separate the target from the features and cast the target to int, Stratified train/test split with random_state=seed, Remove ID, SEX and AGE from the predictors via predictive_features, No scaling for the random forest (StandardScaler is used only in the logistic regression pipeline)

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: The model does not use the documented 0.35 classification threshold, so its labels are not directly comparable with those of the migration candidate, and the cutoff actually applied to its outputs is not documented. Performance metrics, validation results, fairness results for SEX and age groups, and prediction PSI are not available, and no monitoring plan, monitoring thresholds, approval status, data time period or sample representativeness are documented. The model has no parameter-based identity hash because model_identity hashes only Statsmodels parameters; only its feature list is hashed. A synthetic demo dataset with reduced features may be used when the UCI data is unavailable, which would change the inputs relative to the expected 30,000-row UCI data.
